items.readable_text:
Content:
In this lesson, we will learn how to compute the tangent plane to the level surface [MATH: f (x, y, z) = k,] where [MATH: k] is a constant, at some point [MATH: \mathbf x_0 = (x_0, y_0, z_0).]

Content:
As an example, consider the function

Content:
[MATH: f(x,y,z) = x^2 +y^2+z.]

Content:
Suppose that we wish to find the equation of the tangent plane to the level surface that passes through the point where [MATH: (x,y,z)= (1,1, 2).]

Content:
Evaluating [MATH: f] at the point [MATH: (1,1,2),] we get

Content:
[MATH: f(x,y,z) = (1)^2 +(1)^2+2 = 4.]

Content:
So, the equation of our level surface is

Content:
[MATH: x^2 +y^2+z = 4.]

Content:
Now, to find the equation of the tangent plane to this surface at [MATH: (1,1,2),] we can use the following result:

Content:
> Given a hypersurface [MATH: w = f(x,y,z)] and a point [MATH: \mathbf x_0 = (x_0,y_0,z_0)] that lies in the domain of [MATH: f], the gradient [MATH: \nabla \! f (\mathbf x_0)] is normal to the tangent plane of the level surface [MATH: f (x, y, z) = k] at the point [MATH: \mathbf x_0].

Graphic:
[IMG: /graphics/7ac9211e0b4741ea8104801e738b8b2c]

Content:
We can now find the equation of the tangent plane to our level surface.

Content:
First, we find the gradient of [MATH: f(x,y,z)] and evaluate it at [MATH: \mathbf x_0 = (1,1,2)\mathbin{:}]

Content:
[MATH: ∇f(x, y, z)|= f_{x}i + f_{y}j + f_{z}k; = (∂)/(∂x)(x^{2} + y^{2} + z)i + (∂)/(∂y)(x^{2} + y^{2} + z)j + (∂)/(∂z)(x^{2} + y^{2} + z)k; = 2xi + 2yj + k; ∇f(1, 1, 2)|= 2(1)i + 2(1)j + k; = 2i + 2j + k; = ⟨2, 2, 1⟩]

Content:
Finally, we write down the Cartesian equation of the tangent plane:

Content:
[MATH: \eqalign{
\nabla f(x_0,y_0,z_0) \cdot \langle x-x_0, \: y-y_0, \: z-z_0 \rangle & = 0 \[3pt]
\nabla f(1,1,2) \cdot \langle x-1, \: y-1, \: z-2 \rangle & = 0 \[3pt]
\langle 2,\:2,\:1\rangle\cdot \langle x-1, y-1, z-2\rangle &= 0\[3pt]
2(x-1)+ 2(y-1) + (z-2) & =0\
2x +2y +z -6&=0
}]

sections.normalized_html: EXPLANATION
sections.readable_text: EXPLANATION

sections.normalized_html:
The equation of the tangent plane to the level surface [MATH: f(x,y,z) = k] at the point [MATH: (x_0,y_0,z_0)] can be expressed as

[MATH: \nabla \! f(x_0,y_0,z_0) \cdot \langle x-x_0, \: y-y_0, \: z-z_0 \rangle = 0.]

First, we find the gradient of [MATH: f(x,y,z)] and evaluate it at [MATH: (x_0,y_0,z_0) =(2,-2,1)\mathbin{:}]

[MATH: ∇f(x, y, z)|= f_{x}i + f_{y}j + f_{z}k; = (∂)/(∂x)(x^{2} + y^{2} + z^{2})i + (∂)/(∂y)(x^{2} + y^{2} + z^{2})j + (∂)/(∂z)(x^{2} + y^{2} + z^{2})k; = 2xi + 2yj + 2zk; ∇f(2, − 2, 1)|= 2(2)i + 2(− 2)j + 2(1)k; = 4i − 4j + 2k; = ⟨4, − 4, 2⟩]

We can now write down the Cartesian equation of the tangent plane to the level surface, as follows:
[MATH: ∇f(x_{0}, y_{0}, z_{0}) ⋅ ⟨x − x_{0}, y − y_{0}, z − z_{0}⟩|= 0; ∇f(2, − 2, 1) ⋅ ⟨x − 2, y − (− 2), z − 1⟩|= 0; ⟨4, − 4, 2⟩ ⋅ ⟨x − 2, y + 2, z − 1⟩|= 0; 4(x − 2) − 4(y + 2) + 2(z − 1)|= 0; 4x − 4y + 2z − 18|= 0; 2x − 2y + z − 9|= 0]

sections.normalized_html: Consider the surface [MATH: z^3y^2 =x^2-5.] Find the equation of the tangent plane to this surface at the point [MATH: (-1,2,-1).]
sections.readable_text: Consider the surface [MATH: z^3y^2 =x^2-5.] Find the equation of the tangent plane to this surface at the point [MATH: (-1,2,-1).]

sections.normalized_html: EXPLANATION
sections.readable_text: EXPLANATION

sections.normalized_html:
First, we bring all variables to one side:

[MATH: z^{3}y^{2}|= x^{2} − 5; z^{3}y^{2} − x^{2}|= − 5]

If we set [MATH: f(x,y,z) = z^3y^2 - x^2,] our surface can be viewed as the level surface [MATH: f(x,y,z)=-5.]

Recall that the equation of the tangent plane to the level surface [MATH: f(x,y,z) = k] at the point [MATH: (x_0,y_0,z_0)] can be expressed as

[MATH: \nabla f(x_0,y_0,z_0) \cdot \langle x-x_0, \: y-y_0, \: z-z_0 \rangle = 0.]

Now, we find the gradient of [MATH: f(x,y,z)] and evaluate it at [MATH: (-1,2,-1)\mathbin{:}]

[MATH: ∇f(x, y, z)|= f_{x}(x, y, z)i + f_{y}(x, y, z)j + f_{z}(x, y, z)k; = (∂)/(∂x)(z^{3}y^{2} − x^{2})i + (∂)/(∂y)(z^{3}y^{2} − x^{2})j + (∂)/(∂z)(z^{3}y^{2} − x^{2})k; = (− 2x)i + 2z^{3}yj + 3z^{2}y^{2}k; ∇f(− 1, 2, − 1)|= (− 2)(− 1)i + 2(− 1)^{3}(2)j + 3(− 1)^{2}(2)^{2}k; = 2i − 4j + 12k; = ⟨2, − 4, 12⟩]

Finally, we can now write down the Cartesian equation of the tangent plane to the level surface, as follows:

[MATH: ∇f(x_{0}, y_{0}, z_{0}) ⋅ ⟨x − x_{0}, y − y_{0}, z − z_{0}⟩|= 0; ∇f(− 1, 2, − 1) ⋅ ⟨x − (− 1), y − 2, z − (− 1)⟩|= 0; ⟨2, − 4, 12⟩ ⋅ ⟨x + 1, y − 2, z + 1⟩|= 0; 2(x + 1) − 4(y − 2) + 12(z + 1)|= 0; 2x − 4y + 12z + 22|= 0; x − 2y + 6z + 11|= 0]
